questions.question: According to the high‑level overview, why is it important to show the distribution of functions across system modules in the architecture diagram?

options.A: To illustrate the physical layout of hardware components.
options.B: To identify which modules can be developed and tested independently.
options.C: To list all programming languages used in the project.
options.D: To specify the exact timing constraints for each function.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The architecture overview highlights how functions are allocated to modules, which helps teams work on parts independently and plan integration [Page 28].

---

questions.question: Reusing architectural components, as mentioned in the context, primarily helps to:

options.A: Reduce the number of required programmers.
options.B: Ensure that every module has a unique design.
options.C: Decrease development time and improve reliability.
options.D: Increase the total number of system documents.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The text notes that reused components should be reused, implying benefits such as faster development and higher reliability through proven parts [Page 28].

questions.question: In the described testing process for critical systems, what is the main responsibility of the separate testing group?

options.B: Developing tests and maintaining detailed test result records.
options.D: Conducting marketing analysis for the product.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The separate testing group is tasked with creating tests and keeping detailed records of outcomes for critical systems [Page 41].

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the integration stage mentioned on page 49?

options.A: To verify that each component works in isolation.
options.B: To combine components from different team members into a cohesive system.
options.C: To finalize the graphical user interface design.
options.D: To archive older versions of the software.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] Integration involves assembling components developed by various sub‑teams to form the complete system, as noted in the description of system testing [Page 49].

questions.question: Adding tables or graphical models to natural‑language requirements helps stakeholders to:

options.A: Reduce the overall size of the requirements document.
options.B: Visualize computation flow, state changes, and interaction sequences.
options.C: Eliminate the need for any verbal communication.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The context explains that extra information like tables or graphics clarifies how computations proceed and how the system behaves [Page 24].

questions.question: The tabular specification shown for the insulin pump (Figure 4.14) primarily serves to:

options.A: List the brand names of all pump components.
options.B: Detail the step‑by‑step computation of insulin dosage.
options.C: Provide a marketing slogan for the device.
options.D: Outline the manufacturing process of the pump.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The figure is described as a “tabular specification of computation” for the insulin pump, indicating it records dosage calculations [Page 24].

questions.question: Dijkstra’s article “The Humble Programmer” is referenced to emphasize which principle relevant to system architecture?

options.A: The necessity of using low‑level programming languages.
options.B: The importance of modesty and rigorous verification in software development.
options.C: The requirement for every programmer to write documentation.
options.D: The advantage of proprietary code over open source.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Dijkstra’s classic work stresses humility and careful proof, concepts that underpin disciplined architectural design [Page 36].

questions.question: The web link provided (http://software‑engineering‑book.com/web/debugging/) is most likely intended to:

options.A: Offer a downloadable compiler for the project.
options.B: Provide resources and techniques for locating and fixing bugs.
options.C: Host the source code repository for the system.
options.D: Supply licensing information for third‑party libraries.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The URL is placed under a “debugging” heading, indicating it supplies debugging guidance [Page 41].

questions.question: System testing is described as a collective process. Which statement best reflects this characterization?

options.A: Only the lead architect participates in system testing.
options.B: Designers and programmers are excluded from system testing.
options.C: Multiple stakeholders, possibly including a dedicated testing team, work together to evaluate the whole system.
options.D: System testing is performed by a single automated script without human oversight.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The passage notes that system testing involves a collective effort and may include a separate testing team alongside designers and programmers [Page 49].

questions.question: Which of the following stages of development testing most directly involves the integration of components created by different sub‑teams?
questions.explanation: [Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The integration stage is explicitly mentioned as the point where components from different team members are combined before system testing [Page 49].
